approach: Add one module, crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs, with `check_reading_coverage(reading, request)`, wired as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` after `check_scope_limit`. It reads the request's `Acceptance:` section into bullets (a wrapped bullet's continuation lines join it). It reduces each bullet and each criterion to content stems, with no prose-word stripping. A bullet's score against a criterion is the lower of two shares: (A) the share of its stems found, each stem weighted 1/df, where df is the number of the request's bullets containing it; and (B) the share of its distinguishing stems found, meaning its lowest-df stems. A bullet's best criterion is the one with the highest such score. A bullet below the threshold (initially 40 percent, tuned on the fixtures) is omitted. This answers finding 2: a criterion that covers a sibling bullet and shares only its framing words scores 0 on (B), so it cannot cover the dropped bullet. For a one-bullet request, or a bullet whose stems all have the same df, (A) and (B) both equal the plain share, so nothing is discarded or made vacuous. An omitted bullet refuses the reading, naming it, unless the non-bullet text affirmatively allows a split. Split permission now needs a phrase that names the job, request or work being split (finding 1); bare 'split into' and 'split it' are dropped. Readings that ask a question or decline, and requests with no Acceptance heading, are not checked. Tests: unit tests in coverage.rs, the new refusal_corpus cases, the CHANGELOG entry and the doc comment. The fake reader (fake.rs) is expected to need one criterion per Acceptance bullet (finding 4), decided after running the athena-core and athena-agent suites. drain.rs changes only if a cli test fails. The 10% figure stays a labelled estimate. The verification replay over recorded readings measures the real rate against the 15% hold limit, and the CHANGELOG says so (finding 5).

decisions.choice: Score each bullet by min(A,B) against each criterion and take the best criterion. Stems: lowercase alphanumeric runs, a fixed stop list, tokens under 2 characters dropped, then suffix stripping (ing, ed, es, s; only when 3 or more characters remain and the word does not end in ss), then a trailing e dropped and a doubled final consonant after ed/ing collapsed (not l, s, z). (A) = sum of weights of the bullet's stems found in the criterion divided by the sum of weights of all the bullet's stems, with weight = 2520/df using integer division. (B) = the number of the bullet's lowest-df stems found in the criterion divided by the number of those stems. Covered when best*100 >= total*COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT, in integer math (u64), initial value 40.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2 without discarding any word. Take sibling bullets 'The status list shows each job's state' and '...shows each job's duration'. The criterion for the first shares the framing stems with the second, but not 'duration', its only df=1 stem. (B) is then 0, so the dropped bullet is refused. A bullet whose stems all share one df gets a plain share, so no bullet becomes empty or vacuously covered, which was the rejection of 20261029-111121-fzx0. The recorded ttnw pair ('a new test with no Steward or Hestia requests queued asserts the plan order is identical' for 'a test: with no improvement requests queued, ordering is unchanged') and the bp5e pair ('its doc comment names the root cause' for 'The root cause is named in the change description...') are paraphrases. Stemming meets queued/queue, ordering/order, names/named. The tuning test prints every bullet's A, B and score and asserts min covered score >= COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT > max omitted score. The threshold is set from those numbers, not fixed in advance.

rejected.option: Strip words the request prose repeats and require stem uniqueness
rejected.why: The rejected design of 20261029-111121-fzx0: a bullet whose distinguishing words are repeated in the prose becomes empty and is vacuously covered.

rejected.option: Raw-count share against the best single criterion (the round-1 plan)
rejected.why: A sibling's criterion shares the framing words and covers the dropped bullet (finding 2).

rejected.option: idf weights alone with a steeper exponent (1/df^3)
rejected.why: It still fails open once a bullet has about six framing stems against one distinguishing stem. The separate distinguishing-stem share does not depend on how many framing words there are.

rejected.option: One-to-one assignment of criteria to bullets
rejected.why: A single legitimate criterion that covers two bullets would leave one of them uncovered, which wrongly refuses readings that cover every bullet.

rejected.option: A model call to judge coverage
rejected.why: Reading checks are deterministic and call no model (checks.rs doc comments).

decisions.choice: Parse the Acceptance section line by line, untrimmed. The section starts after a line that is 'Acceptance:' or 'Acceptance criteria:' (trimmed, case-insensitive, leading # or * ignored). A line whose trimmed text passes `is_bullet` starts a bullet. A non-empty non-bullet line directly after a bullet or its continuation (no blank line between) is joined to that bullet when it is indented, or when the previous line does not end in '.', '!', '?' or ':' and the line is not a heading (a line ending in ':' or starting 'Files:' or 'Priority:'). Blank lines are skipped. The section ends at a heading line, or at a non-bullet line that follows a blank line.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. A hard-wrapped bullet is scored on its whole text and the bullets after it are still checked. Requests with no Acceptance heading are not checked. Many existing requests and tests carry bare bullets (job_plan.rs:166; the corpus cases star-bullets and numbered-dot-parts), and checking them would refuse lists the owner never marked as acceptance. `is_bullet` (topics.rs:266) is reused read-only, so `request_text_acceptance` and `athena plan` do not change.

rejected.option: End the section at the first non-bullet line (the round-1 design)
rejected.why: A wrapped bullet's continuation ends the section and the later bullets go unchecked.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet in the request as acceptance, as `request_text_acceptance` does
rejected.why: It widens the refusal rate far past the estimate and refuses plain lists.

decisions.choice: A request allows a split only when a sentence of its non-bullet text (split by the existing `sentences`, lowercased, curly apostrophes made straight) both (a) has a whole-phrase match (`has_phrase`) on a phrase that names what is split, and (b) has no negation token and no '?'. The phrases are the modals ('may', 'can', 'could', 'free to', 'allowed to', 'ok to', 'okay to', 'is allowed to') followed by 'split' and a job object ('this job', 'the job', 'this request', 'the request', 'this work', 'the work', 'it into jobs', 'it into parts', 'it into follow-ups', 'it into separate jobs', 'into separate jobs', 'into follow-up jobs', 'into follow-ups'). The imperative 'split this job', 'split the job', 'split this request' and 'split the request' also count. Negation tokens: not, never, no, cannot, without, avoid, forbid, forbidden, instead of, and any word ending in n't (and 'dont'). 'must' is not a negation.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. Ordinary code prose ('Split the log line into fields', 'split it on commas', 'Split the output into two columns') names no job, request or work, so it matches no phrase and the check stays on. 'Do not split this job' has a negation and allows nothing. 'Should we split this job?' is a question and allows nothing. The phrase table in the unit test has false-positive rows as well as negations. A corpus case puts 'Split the output into two columns.' in the prose with a dropped bullet and expects a refusal.

rejected.option: Keep bare 'split into' and 'split it' and the bare 'split is fine' forms
rejected.why: They match code-prose and turn the check off for the whole request (finding 1).

rejected.option: Any occurrence of the word 'split' allows a split
rejected.why: 'Do not split this job' would disable the check, the sza7 failure.

risks.risk: The two-share score refuses a reading that covers a bullet by paraphrase. This happens when the bullet shares most stems with siblings and its few distinguishing stems are reworded, for example 'duration' written as 'elapsed time'. That would raise the refusal rate above the 10% estimate.
risks.mitigation: The refusal names the bullet and its score, so the reader's one correction is to use the bullet's words. The tuning table prints A, B and the score for every recorded shape, and the ttnw and bp5e paraphrases must pass. The verification replay over recorded readings measures the real rate against the 15% hold limit. If it is exceeded the job is held, and the producer's loop replay figure, if available, replaces 10.

risks.risk: A criterion that covers two bullets at once, or a reading that merges bullets, is refused because the distinguishing-stem share of one bullet is low.
risks.mitigation: Scoring is per criterion, so a merged criterion that contains both bullets' distinguishing stems scores high for both. A reading that wants fewer, larger criteria can still ask the split or merge as a question, which is not checked.

risks.risk: A closing sentence directly under the last bullet, with no blank line, is joined to that bullet and lowers its score.
risks.mitigation: Joining stops at a blank line, a heading, or a previous line that ends a sentence. The wrapped-bullet test pins both the join and the stop. The refusal text shows the bullet text it scored.

risks.risk: The recorded sza7, ttnw and bp5e texts are not available, because records/ is absent. The fixtures use only the brief's quoted fragments and rebuilt framing, so the tuned threshold rests on a small sample.
risks.mitigation: Each fixture is labelled 'rebuilt, records absent', as the corpus does. The sibling fixture is deliberately realistic, with shared framing. The verification replay runs the real rule over recorded readings and holds the job above 15%.

risks.risk: The phrase list misses some affirmative split wordings and refuses a request whose owner allowed a split.
risks.mitigation: A refused reading can ask the split as a question, which is not checked. The phrase table pins the accepted and refused forms, including the code-prose lookalikes.

risks.risk: The corpus INPUT_FORMS array is fixed-size. A forgotten length bump or an unused tag fails `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms`.
risks.mitigation: Step 7 sets the length to 62 for ten new tags, and each tag is carried by a case named in the plan. The demonstration for criterion 5 runs the corpus test.

risks.risk: The fake reader and hestia, steward or cli tests fail after the check is wired.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 runs the athena-agent, athena-core and workspace suites and applies the per-bullet fake criteria. Criterion 10 limits the diff to fake.rs and drain.rs.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs. The sza7 request is rebuilt with realistic shared framing: three Acceptance bullets that all open 'The status list shows each job's ...', the last about duration. It is labelled 'rebuilt, records absent'. A reading that omits the duration bullet goes through `check_reading_coverage`. A reading with a criterion for each of the three bullets goes through it too. A second sibling-framing fixture, with only the first bullet covered, is also run.
demonstrations.observes: The omitting reading returns Err whose text contains the duration bullet and the phrase 'acceptance bullet'. The sibling fixture returns Err naming the uncovered sibling, which the plain-share scorer of round 1 would have accepted. The reading covering all bullets returns Ok. `refusing_check` names `check_reading_coverage` as the refuser. The final line is 'test result: ok'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, or if the bullet is not named, the Err assertion fails. If the scorer used a plain share, the sibling fixture would be accepted and its Err assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `check_reading_coverage` (added by step 2), reached through `refusing_check` (exists, checks.rs:518). The fixture is a local `fn reading(criteria: &[&str]) -> Reading` in the coverage.rs tests module (added by step 5). It builds a Reading as the corpus `base_reading` does (refusal_corpus.rs:161), and `use super::*` reaches `Reading`. It passes criteria as plain strings. The scoring is not duplicated in the test.

demonstrations.method: The test `coverage_accepts_the_recorded_ttnw_and_bp5e_paraphrases` loads the ttnw and bp5e request and reading shapes. The bullet and criterion strings are the ones quoted in the brief, copied verbatim. The rest of each request is rebuilt, and the source is labelled. It runs `check_reading_coverage` on each. `coverage_threshold_is_tuned_on_the_recorded_shapes` prints each bullet's A, B and score.
demonstrations.observes: Zero refusals. The printed scores for ttnw and bp5e are at or above COVERAGE_MIN_PERCENT. The tuning test asserts the lowest covered score >= the threshold > the highest omitted score, over the ttnw, bp5e, sza7 and sibling shapes.
demonstrations.fails_without: A scorer that does not stem queued/queue, ordering/order and names/named, or a threshold above the covered scores, refuses these shapes and the zero-refusal assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` and the pure scorer `coverage_gaps(request, criteria)`, both added by step 2. The fixtures are consts in the coverage.rs tests module (step 5). They are injected as plain strings. The plan assumes records/ is absent from the snapshot, so only the quoted fragments are exact.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_judges_words_the_prose_repeats`. The request prose says 'the duration column shows seconds', and one bullet is 'The duration column shows seconds'. Reading A has criteria only for the other bullets. Reading B adds a criterion containing 'duration', 'column' and 'seconds'. Both go through `check_reading_coverage`.
demonstrations.observes: A returns Err naming the bullet. B returns Ok. The bullet's words are scored even though the prose repeats them.
demonstrations.fails_without: The rejected design that strips prose-repeated words leaves the bullet with no words, so A is accepted and the Err assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` (step 2) with the local `reading()` fixture (step 5). The request is a const string in the test.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_a_split_is_allowed_only_when_affirmed`. The same request is run with 'You may split this job.', with 'Do not split this job.', with 'Split the output into two columns.' and with no split line, each against a reading that covers fewer bullets. `request_allows_split` is also run over a phrase table. Allowed rows: 'You may split this job.'; 'Feel free to split this job into follow-ups.'; 'It is ok to split the request into separate jobs.'. Refused rows: 'Do not split this job', 'never split it into jobs', 'don't split the job', "can't split this job", 'without splitting', 'Should we split this job?', 'Split the log line into fields.', 'split it on commas', 'Split the output into two columns.'.
demonstrations.observes: Only the affirmative request returns Ok. The negated, silent and code-prose requests return Err naming the dropped bullet. The table gives the expected booleans.
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule that treats any 'split', 'split into' or 'split it' as permission accepts 'Do not split this job' or the code-prose rows, so an Err assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` and `request_allows_split`, both added by step 2. The local `reading()` fixture and const requests are added by step 5. Corpus cases coverage-split-allowed-accepted, coverage-split-negated-refused and coverage-split-lookalike-prose-refused (step 7) run the same shapes through `refusing_check`.

demonstrations.method: Step 7 adds corpus cases. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` extracts the `step!(check_` names from `reading_source()` (refusal_corpus.rs, where step 7 adds coverage.rs) and fails unless `check_reading_coverage` is the refusing check in at least one case. `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` checks the new tags. Also run the Grep pattern `step!\(check_reading_coverage\(reading, request\)\);` on crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs. It must match exactly once.
demonstrations.observes: All corpus tests pass. The refusing cases are coverage-omitted-bullet-sza7-refused, coverage-sibling-framing-refused, coverage-star-bullet-omitted-refused, coverage-number-dot-omitted-refused, coverage-wrapped-bullet-omitted-refused, coverage-prose-repeated-words-refused, coverage-split-negated-refused and coverage-split-lookalike-prose-refused. The Grep shows one match.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line, `refusing_check` never names `check_reading_coverage` and the refusing-case expectations fail. Without a case, the every-check-has-a-case test fails.
demonstrations.seam: `refusing_check` (exists, checks.rs:518) and the corpus harness `cases()` and `run()` (exist). The new cases are built with the existing `case()` helper (exists, refusal_corpus.rs:230) and `base_reading()`, with a criterion removed from `case.reading.acceptance_criteria`. `Case.reading` is a pub field of the struct, so no harness change is needed. The cases are added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks on the final tree, run as separate commands if the verifier allows only whole simple commands.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: No fmt diff, no clippy warning, all tests pass. These include every existing refusal_corpus case, the reading.rs order and doc tests, the athena-agent fake.rs tests, and the athena-core and athena-cli tests that use the deterministic fake reader.
demonstrations.fails_without: A step-order break, an unused import, a corpus case that an earlier check now refuses, or a fake-reader refusal in a hestia, steward or cli test fails one of the three.
demonstrations.seam: The whole workspace. No seam is added.

demonstrations.method: Test `coverage_replay_over_the_recorded_shapes` runs `check_reading_coverage` over the ttnw, bp5e and sza7 shapes, the sibling-framing shape, and the corpus shapes with an Acceptance heading (steward-three-dash-bullets and root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying). It also runs a copy of each with one bullet dropped. It prints 'coverage replay: N readings, R refused, refused 0 readings that cover every bullet'. It asserts every refusal is an omission, no covering reading is refused, and R equals the number of dropped-bullet readings. The corpus test `reading_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended` reads the declared share with `replay_declaration` and expects Some(10). The limit is `replay_limit_percent(Some(10))` = 15.
demonstrations.observes: The printed replay line, and a declared share of 10 with a hold limit of 15. The CHANGELOG and criterion text say that 10 is an estimate, that the printed figure covers fixtures only, and that the verification replay measures the real rate over recorded readings and holds the job above 15%.
demonstrations.fails_without: A scorer that refuses a covered paraphrase fails the no-covered-reading-refused assertion. A criterion without the exact 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' form makes `replay_declaration` return no share.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_coverage` and `replay_declaration` (exists, replay.rs:263). The fixture list is a const array in the coverage.rs tests (step 5). The corpus request strings are read from the corpus file's `cases()`, which is the test's input and not a double. No history replay exists in the snapshot, so the figure is over fixtures.

demonstrations.method: New test `reading_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended` follows `history_fixture_refusal_is_declared_intended`. It collapses white space in `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` and asserts the substrings 'check_reading_coverage', 'refuses more readings', 'higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 10% of newly refused readings', 'estimate' and 'verification replay'.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` holds the new entry under Added.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing entry or a changed phrase fails an assertion.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!` of CHANGELOG.md, a pattern already used in this file. The test is added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: The same new test reads the contiguous `///` lines above `pub fn check_reading_coverage(` from `reading_source()` (with coverage.rs added by step 7). It asserts the needles '20261029-084645-sza7', '[`check_reading_acceptance`]', 'a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet', 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'estimate'.
demonstrations.observes: All needles are present in the doc comment.
demonstrations.fails_without: If coverage.rs is not in `reading_source()`, the doc is not found and the assertions fail. A missing needle fails.
demonstrations.seam: `reading_source()` (exists in refusal_corpus.rs), extended by step 7. The doc text is written by step 2.

demonstrations.method: After `cargo test --locked` passes, run `git status` and `git diff --stat`.
demonstrations.observes: The changed paths are a subset of the seven deliverables. fake.rs appears only if the athena-core, athena-agent or athena-cli suite failed without it, and then its diff is only the added per-bullet criteria. drain.rs appears only if a cli test still failed after the fake.rs change.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unneeded edit to either file shows up as an extra changed path.
